mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS below 3.0%) compresses discount rates and boosts equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE above 5.0%) signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE is above 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in labor market strength (PAYEMS) and housing demand (HOUST) indicates a broad-based economic slowdown, which triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decline > 0.5% and HOUST decline > 0.5% in the prior month
failure_condition: When PAYEMS and HOUST both decline by more than 0.5% in the prior month, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a housing market recovery phase (HOUST above 1000.0), the S&P 500 tends to produce positive returns over the next 60 days as housing activity supports consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: In periods when HOUST is above 1000.0, the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates strengthening supply-side activity, which supports corporate profitability and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO is above its 12-month moving average, the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% annually signals inflationary pressures that prompt the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL is above 2.5% annually, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of a rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and accelerating inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicates an active monetary tightening cycle, which causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25pp and CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5pp in the last month
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25pp and CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5pp in the last month, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a strong labor market (PAYEMS above 137000.0), the S&P 500 tends to produce positive returns over the next 5 days as robust employment supports consumer spending and corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: In periods when PAYEMS is above 137000.0, the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.
